record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: When n = 1 and α is of constant type, it is known that U_α is open near 0 in the Sobolev topology W^{4,p} for p > 1. Does the same openness statement remain true for p = 1, i.e. in W^{4,1}?

evidence.quote: The author has been unable to decide if this is also true when p = 1 !

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Diff}^r(\mathbb{T}^1)$ denote the group of orientation-preserving $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of the circle $\mathbb{T}^1=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For an irrational number $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, let $R_\alpha:\mathbb{T}^1\to\mathbb{T}^1$ denote the rigid rotation $x\mapsto x+\alpha$, and define
\[
U_\alpha=\{\,f\in\mathrm{Diff}^\infty(\mathbb{T}^1):\ f\text{ is smoothly conjugate to }R_\alpha\,\}.
\]
Recall that $\alpha$ is of constant type if the partial quotients $(a_n)$ in its continued fraction expansion are bounded.

Identify a neighborhood of $0$ in the space of perturbations of $R_\alpha$ with a neighborhood in the Sobolev space $W^{4,p}(\mathbb{T}^1)$ via $f=R_\alpha+u$ with $u\in W^{4,p}(\mathbb{T}^1)$. It is known that, when $\alpha$ is of constant type, the set $U_\alpha$ is a neighborhood of $0$ in the topology of $W^{4,p}(\mathbb{T}^1)$ for every $p>1$.

Question: Does the same openness statement hold in the borderline case $p=1$? That is, when $\alpha$ is of constant type, is $U_\alpha$ a neighborhood of $0$ in the $W^{4,1}(\mathbb{T}^1)$ topology?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of the borderline $W^{4,1}$ openness question for $U_\alpha$ when $\alpha$ is of constant type. Related works on Herman's theory and KAM regularity for circle diffeomorphisms (Yoccoz, Khanin–Sinai, Katznelson–Ornstein) address smoothness of conjugacies but not this specific endpoint Sobolev openness, so the status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Herman's Theory Revisited (Khanin)
status_evidence.snippet: Sharp regularity of conjugacies for Diophantine rotation numbers, but does not address $W^{4,1}$ endpoint openness.
status_evidence.claim: Related KAM/Herman regularity results do not settle the $p=1$ Sobolev openness question.

status_evidence.title: Sur la conjugaison différentiable des difféomorphismes du cercle à des rotations (Herman)
status_evidence.snippet: Foundational result on smooth conjugation of circle diffeomorphisms to rotations.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational background; does not resolve the $W^{4,1}$ borderline openness.
